content.comment_body: Hello. Is there any functionality or service in [product_name] to upload a program to a [product_name] controller from another application? I want to build an application that uploads a user program to the [product_name] controller and am wondering if [product_name] offers a service, command line tool, or other feature to connect my application for program upload. Thanks.
I'm not sure I understand your question. Could you please give a more specific example?

It seems you're asking if it's possible to upload a [product_name] project file to a device using command line actions, without manually using a mouse and keyboard. I've looked for this option as well. For example, something like: [product_name].exe --address=192.168.0.1 -upload=MyFile.lsc would launch [product_name], read the file, upload it to the device, and then exit (including error status). Ideally, this would work without starting the graphical interface. On Linux, many utilities support command line options for progress tracking in text mode.
Exactly, that's what I'm looking for. Thanks [user_name].

There's mention on this site of a protocol called PG for downloading, uploading, starting, and stopping a controller: [url]. Is the PG protocol available? Can it be used to download files and start the controller?

No, [company_name] does not release such information. Only [product_name] (it would be much better if upload/download/start/stop via command line were possible). Unfortunately, don't expect this feature. [company_name] does not prioritize this and there are long-standing firmware and software issues that remain unfixed.
I think command line communication might not be possible with the controller due to password transfer requirements.

Password protection for LSC files is a newer feature, only supported in versions [version_no] and [version_no], and it's not mandatory for access control. Also, adding a password from the command line wouldn't be an issue if the functionality exists. Example: [product_name].exe --address=192.168.0.1 --password=LOGO file=MyFile.lsc
That's actually incorrect. LSC password access is present only starting from [version_no].
Okay, I don't have [version_no] available at the moment. Either way, password protection for LSC files is relatively new and not required.
Honestly, the idea of my system being wiped out by an external command line is concerning. It's understandable that access is limited to specialized software for controllers.

What's the distinction? Having command line options doesn't make [product_name] anything other than a specialized controller tool. Is program upload or stopping via command line more risky than through mouse or keyboard in the GUI? I doubt it.

analysis.insight_summary: Users want a way to upload programs to a [product_name] controller programmatically, preferably through command line features in [product_name], eliminating the need for manual graphical interface use. The absence of such options or available APIs is a common frustration, especially for automation and scripting. Concerns were noted about password protection in newer software versions and limited technical access protocols.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to find a method in [product_name] that enables programmatic or command line program uploads to [product_name] controllers, avoiding the graphical user interface.
